clues.title: Huge round crater
clues.data: Basin 62 km wide. Rock was thrown out to the north-east, so the hit came from the south-west.
clues.dataCadet: A giant round hole. Rock was thrown out all on one side, like a splash!

clues.title: Glass beads
clues.data: Tiny glass beads around the rim: rock that melted in a flash and froze in mid-air.
clues.dataCadet: Little glass beads everywhere. Something melted rock in an instant.

clues.title: Iridium spike
clues.data: A thin dark layer with 120× normal iridium, a metal rare in surface rock but common in asteroids.
clues.dataCadet: A thin dark stripe full of a rare metal that asteroids carry.

clues.title: Ordinary air
clues.data: N₂ 78%, O₂ 19%, CO₂ 0.9%. Thin, fairly ordinary air. Nothing that would trap lots of heat.
clues.dataCadet: The air is pretty normal. Not much heat-trapping gas.

clues.title: Warm vents
clues.data: Vents at 60 °C, but the rock below is old and cold. No fresh lava for ages.
clues.dataCadet: Warm steam, but the ground underneath is old and cold.

clues.title: Normal radiation
clues.data: Radiation is normal for a world this far from its star.
clues.dataCadet: Radiation is normal here.

clues.title: Two cities
clues.data: One Orrin city lies BELOW the iridium layer. A second, rebuilt city lies ABOVE it.
clues.dataCadet: There's an old city under the dark stripe and a newer city on top!

explanations.impact: The crater, glass beads and iridium layer all point to an asteroid strike.
explanations.greenhouse: The air here is thin and ordinary, so it couldn't trap much heat.
explanations.stellar: Radiation readings were normal, so the star wasn't the problem here. At least, not yet.
explanations.volcanism: The vents are warm, but the rock below is old and cold. No big eruptions for ages.
explanations.unknown: Fair! Saying 'we need more data' is real science. Mission Control will send what they know.

layers.prompt: Put the layers in order from TOP (newest) to BOTTOM (oldest).

glyph.prompt: The Orrin count in dots. What comes next?

clues.title: CO₂ blanket
clues.data: Atmosphere 96% CO₂, about 90× thicker than Earth's, with sulfuric-acid clouds.
clues.dataCadet: The air is almost all carbon dioxide, a gas that traps heat. And it's super thick!

clues.title: Oven world
clues.data: Surface 460 °C, almost the same day and night, pole to equator. Heat is trapped everywhere.
clues.dataCadet: It's 460 °C everywhere, day AND night. The heat can't escape.

clues.title: Lost oceans
clues.data: Ripple marks and salt layers: this basin was a sea. The water is gone.
clues.dataCadet: Ripples and salt, so this was once a sea!

clues.title: Isotope clock
clues.data: Radioactive clock in the salt: the seas dried up slowly over ~1 billion years while starlight kept rising.
clues.dataCadet: A natural clock in the salt says the seas dried slowly while the starlight got stronger.

clues.title: Sleeping volcano
clues.data: Cold summit. The lava flows are hundreds of millions of years old.
clues.dataCadet: The volcano is cold and asleep, and has been for ages.

clues.title: Sulfur rock
clues.data: Rocks rich in sulfur: volcanoes were active long ago.
clues.dataCadet: Smelly sulfur rocks. Volcanoes were busy long ago.

clues.title: Few craters
clues.data: Very few craters. Old lava paved over the surface long ago.
clues.dataCadet: Hardly any craters. Old lava covered them up.

explanations.greenhouse: Thick CO₂ traps heat, the oceans boiled away, and the salt clock shows it happened as the starlight rose. A runaway greenhouse.
explanations.impact: There are hardly any craters, so no giant impact here.
explanations.stellar: Close! The star's rising light started it, but what's cooking Veil now is its thick heat-trapping air.
explanations.volcanism: Volcanoes added gas long ago, but they're cold now and can't explain heat that's still trapped today.
explanations.unknown: Honest answer. Mission Control will send data that helps.

glyph.prompt: Orrin bars: | = 1, ‖ = 2 … They count in twos (binary). What's next?

clues.title: Radiation flood
clues.data: UV and X-ray dose 40× higher than the Orrin domes were designed for.
clues.dataCadet: WAY more harsh starlight than the Orrin buildings were made for.

clues.title: Changed star
clues.data: Today the star is larger, redder and brighter than in Orrin carvings.
clues.dataCadet: The star today is bigger and redder than in Orrin pictures.

clues.title: Rushed shields
clues.data: Shield domes built in a hurry, all facing the star.
clues.dataCadet: Shield domes built fast, all pointing at the star.

clues.title: Sterile soil
clues.data: Soil sterilized 2 m down. Nothing survived near the surface.
clues.dataCadet: The soil is cleaned out deep down. Nothing could live there.

clues.title: Last frost
clues.data: Ice survives only in permanently shadowed craters.
clues.dataCadet: The only ice left hides in dark crater shadows.

clues.title: Air blown away
clues.data: Almost no air left, only thin traces of argon.
clues.dataCadet: Almost no air left at all.

clues.title: Small craters
clues.data: Only small craters. Nothing big enough to end a civilization.
clues.dataCadet: Only little craters here.

clues.title: Lava-tube shelters
clues.data: Old, cold lava tubes, used by the Orrin as shelters.
clues.dataCadet: Old lava tunnels the Orrin hid in.

explanations.stellar: The star itself changed. It grew brighter and redder until its light scoured Hollow clean.
explanations.greenhouse: There's almost no air left to trap heat. Something stripped it away.
explanations.impact: The craters are all small. Not a world-ending hit.
explanations.volcanism: The lava tubes are ancient and cold. The Orrin just used them as shelter.
explanations.unknown: Good instinct to wait for more data. Mission Control can help.
